metadata.title: What Does a P-Value Actually Mean?
metadata.primary_source: Wasserstein & Lazar (2016), The ASA Statement on p-Values, The American Statistician 70(2):129-133, doi:10.1080/00031305.2016.1154108
metadata.reformat: full-length; native portrait graphics; preserve source framing

short_validation.note: B01/B03/B04/B06/B11 authored as native portrait Manim scenes in vertical/scenes.py

beats.narration_text: Hi — Bella, in for Gomathy. A study says p is zero point zero three. Meaning?

show.event: composer sits empty, spark idle
the ask types itself into the composer
send arms
three output lines land — the ask lands answered

props.segment: What Does a P-Value Actually Mean?
props.command: What does a p-value actually mean?
output: It assumes there's no real effect.
Then asks how likely data this extreme is.
Small p: unlikely under that assumption.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer beat: three short typed lines on a mostly-cream page (house exemption named in final_frame_check.py's sparse_by_design_beats() docstring).

beats.narration_text: A p-value isn't the chance you're right. It's how likely data this extreme would be if there were no real effect.

show.event: 'A p-value is' / 'the chance you're right.' types in on two lines
'the chance you're right.' dims and backspaces out
'how likely data this extreme is' / 'if there's no real effect.' types in its place

beats.portrait_note: native portrait Manim restack of the landscape scene (vertical/scenes.py); same text and numbers, ink only, labels >= size 32

qc.sparse_reason: FormBCard's card grid for 2-3 short items doesn't reach 55% fill by design (same characteristic as the passing FormBCard beats in knowledge-cutoff and claude-liam-context-window).

beats.narration_text: First, assume no effect — the null hypothesis — and that the model holds.

show.event: title 'Assume first' settles
items reveal in order: Null hypothesis, The model

beats.narration_text: If the null is true, how often would data this extreme, or more, turn up? That share is the p-value.

show.event: title 'If the Null Is True'; bell curve draws; ILLUSTRATIVE label
'Your data' marker drops onto the curve's right side
the tail beyond the marker shades in; 'At least this extreme'
'Shaded share = p-value' lands under the curve

beats.portrait_note: native portrait Manim restack of the landscape scene (vertical/scenes.py); same text and numbers, ink only, labels >= size 32

beats.narration_text: Nine heads in ten fair flips? Nine or more: about one percent.

show.event: title 'Is This Coin Fair?'; ILLUSTRATIVE label
ten coin tiles flip in: nine H, one T
typeset P(X ≥ 9) = 11/1024 ≈ 0.011 writes in
'About 1% — if the coin is fair' settles beneath

beats.portrait_note: native portrait Manim restack of the landscape scene (vertical/scenes.py); same text and numbers, ink only, labels >= size 32

qc.sparse_reason: FormBCard's card grid for 2-3 short items doesn't reach 55% fill by design (same characteristic as the passing FormBCard beats in knowledge-cutoff and claude-liam-context-window).

beats.narration_text: It's not the chance you're right, nor the effect's size or importance.

show.event: title 'What it doesn't measure' settles
items reveal in order: Chance you're right, Effect size, Importance

beats.narration_text: A huge study can give a tiny effect a tiny p. A small study can give a big effect a large p.

show.event: title 'A Small p Isn't a Big Effect'; ILLUSTRATIVE label
left card: 'Huge study', 50,000 per group, effect 0.2 points, p ≈ 0.002
right card: 'Small study', 10 per group, effect 5 points, p ≈ 0.28

beats.portrait_note: native portrait Manim restack of the landscape scene (vertical/scenes.py); same text and numbers, ink only, labels >= size 32

qc.sparse_reason: FormBCard's card grid for 2-3 short items doesn't reach 55% fill by design (same characteristic as the passing FormBCard beats in knowledge-cutoff and claude-liam-context-window).

beats.narration_text: And p under zero point zero five isn't proof. Never decide on a threshold alone.

show.event: title 'No bright line' settles
items reveal in order: Not proof by itself, Don't decide on a cutoff

qc.sparse_reason: FormBCard's card grid for 2-3 short items doesn't reach 55% fill by design (same characteristic as the passing FormBCard beats in knowledge-cutoff and claude-liam-context-window).

beats.narration_text: Report the effect size, its uncertainty, and every test you ran.

show.event: title 'Report with it' settles
items reveal in order: Effect size, Its uncertainty, Every test run

qc.sparse_reason: FormBCard's card grid for 2-3 short items doesn't reach 55% fill by design (same characteristic as the passing FormBCard beats in knowledge-cutoff and claude-liam-context-window).

beats.narration_text: Summary: how likely your data is with no real effect. Not proof, not size.

show.event: title 'Summary' settles
items reveal in order: Likely under the null?, Not proof, not size

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: explain this result's p-value plainly, and what it doesn't tell me. Check: does it give effect size?

show.event: greeting reads 'Your turn.'
the suggested prompt types into the composer
send arms
